messages:
alex.chen: heads-up — legal asked for a short examples section for handling EU DSARs on audit log exports. can we add a tiny de-id snippet and a recommended wording blurb?
priya.singh: sure. want the wording to live under /docs/security/audit-exports or inline under retention?
morgan: prefer a short subsection under audit-exports called 'Responding to DSARs (EU)'. links to procedure + code example.
rio: +1. keep it prescriptive: what we return, what we redact, and what the timeline is. legal needs to approve exact phrasing though.
sara.legal: thanks for looping me in. we just need two things: (1) clear statement we redact direct identifiers from exports, and (2) a note about minimal data retention windows for EU requests. short and plain language.
alex.chen: draft I cooked up: "When responding to Data Subject Access Requests (EU), we provide a redacted export of audit events limited to the requested time range and event types. We remove direct identifiers (examples below) and provide an explanation of redaction applied." ok to iterate?
priya.singh: looks good. can you add a tiny code snippet that shows recommended field-level removal? e.g. remove ip/email/user_id.
alex.chen: added snippet in PR — see below. it's intentionally language-agnostic.
```
# example de-identification pseudocode
redact_fields = ["ip_address", "email", "user_id", "remote_address"]
def redact(record):
    for f in redact_fields:
        if f in record:
            record[f] = "<redacted>"
    return record
```
priya.singh: perfect. also include guidance that exports to customers should be delivered over an encrypted channel and listed in the DSAR audit record (who requested, who delivered).
morgan: can we add a short note on non-reversible hashing vs removal? e.g. allow hashing for internal analysis but still count as PID removal for DSARs?
sara.legal: prefer removal or irreversible hashing with salt stored separately under KMS. if including hashing example, clarify it is not reversible without KMS access and include retention rationale.
rio: I'll add a short example sentence: "Where necessary for analysis, irreversible hashing (with KMS-managed salt) may be used instead of removing fields; include justification in the DSAR delivery record."
docs-bot: PR opened by alex.chen: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4827 — draft wording + code snippet added. CI: docs-lint passed.
priya.singh: tagging this for review: @sara.legal @morgan — quick review please, especially for the 'examples below' list.
sara.legal: tiny edit suggestion: replace "direct identifiers" with "personal identifiers (e.g., email, phone, IP address)" — more explicit.
alex.chen: updated in PR. pushed.
morgan: LGTM for technical side. one ask: add a short checkbox list in the doc for the DSAR response playbook: confirmation fields redacted, export timeframe, delivery channel, reviewer initials.
priya.singh: good idea. I'll add that to the subsection.
rio: can we add one compliance note: "Do not include system-level debug dumps that may contain extra PID (cookies, tokens)" — flagged as `must not export` in bold.
sara.legal: approved subject to that 'must not export' language and the explicit PID examples. thanks everyone.
docs-bot: PR 4827 approved by sara.legal and morgan, merging in 5m unless objections. :party_popper:
alex.chen: thanks all — will follow up with a short changelog entry for the compliance owners.
